text:
Predicates:
TwinOrTriplet(x) ::: x is either a twin or triplet.
SpendsTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
SameAgeSiblings(x, y) ::: x and y have siblings who are the same age.
ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LivesAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopsStrongBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with family members.
Sibling(x, y) ::: y is a sibling of x.
Age(x, y) ::: x and y are of the same age.

Premises:
∀x (TwinOrTriplet(x) → SpendsTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
∀x ∀y (SameAgeSiblings(x, y) → TwinOrTriplet(x) ∨ TwinOrTriplet(y)) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(x) → ∃y (Sibling(x, y) ∧ SameAgeSiblings(x, y))) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LivesAtHomeRegularly(x) → ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(x)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
∀x (SpendsTimeWithSiblings(x) → ¬LivesAtHomeRegularly(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
( (TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ DevelopsStrongBonds(luke)) ∨ (¬TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(luke)) ) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or neither.

Conclusion:
ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(luke)
